# Single user-directed folding attempt

Use only the RAX robot MCP tools. This is one live attempt, not training,
exploration across episodes, a benchmark batch, or a scripted smoke test.
Read the task and action contract supplied in the launch prompt. Start exactly
one episode. Inspect the actual camera images and measured robot state, decide
an action, execute it, inspect the returned images, and revise your next action.
You choose the manipulation order and all Cartesian/gripper commands. There is
no hidden fold skill, fixed-order controller, or automatic latch.

No files, shell, subagents, external perception, resets, or second episode.
Do not infer motion from commands: compare measured TCP poses and images.
Use deliberate approach orientations, clearance from the table, and short
synchronized action chunks. If repeated actions fail to move the robot, inspect
feedback and change strategy; stop honestly if physically blocked.
Call evaluate before finishing. The physical-lock guard is deliberately false:
report visible/physical progress separately, never claim verified locked success.
The launcher enforces the approved request, token, cost, and wall-time caps.
A cap rejection ends this attempt; do not bypass it or request continuation.
</system-reminder>

Perform the single user-requested long-horizon box-folding attempt through RAX now. Use the actual robot MCP tools directly, not a local fixed script. Start exactly one episode, inspect images/proprioception, choose and execute physical actions, inspect returned observations, and adapt. There is no predefined folding order or ready-made fold skill. You may attempt grasping and folding; do not stop after a free-space smoke move. Observe actual motion and IK residuals; break unreachable targets into reachable waypoints. Use both hands as needed. Do not repeat ineffective actions blindly. Do not call files, shell, subagents, training, resets, or a second episode. A budget rejection ends the attempt. Evaluate and finish when done or physically blocked. Keep narration concise and never claim locking that was not verified.

# Current plain cardboard folding task

Attempt to fold the currently loaded video-inspired connected-lid box with the
existing two Dexmate arms and parallel jaws, through actual contact. The blank
starts flat on the existing table. It has no blue grasp aids. It is an engineering
reconstruction, not a manufacturer-measured dieline or a demonstrated solution.

Public design: 300 x 220 mm base crease spans, 90 mm walls, 4 mm rigid panels,
400 g/m2 areal mass; 14 panels and 13 passive creases. Four body walls, four
front/back corner flaps, a connected lid, two lid-side flaps, lid-front flap,
and a hinged tongue with a real front-wall slot. Total mass is 0.1074308 kg.
No box joint has an actuator. Crease resistance and contact properties are
provisional engineering assumptions. Do not change them.

Work toward stabilizing the blank, forming walls and inward corners, an open
box, then folded lid flaps, lid closure and tongue insertion. You must decide
an accessible order from images, not follow a hard-coded joint sequence.
Either arm may stabilize or fold. No debug poses, object teleportation, welds,
attachments, snapping, artificial supports, or direct object-joint commands.

Observe the back, head and wrist images and robot proprioception. Hidden box
coordinates/joint angles are not supplied to the model. Robot tools return
measured poses, timing and IK residuals; a requested pose is not proof it was reached.

Existing task success requires relative wall/corner/lid geometry, whole-section
tab/slot relationships, low speed, released persistence, acceptable penetration,
and independently verified physical retention. Physical locking is unvalidated;
the existing final success guard remains false. Attempt manipulation honestly,
report actual progress and blockers, and never substitute visual closure for
locked assembly success. One episode only; no training, exploration campaign,
controller submission, or benchmark batch. The existing simulation horizon is
90 seconds; cloud/request/wall limits may end the attempt sooner.


# Existing Dexmate action contract

Dexmate Vega 1 U, two 7-joint arms and two coupled DexGripper S jaws; 16 robot
actuators. Base, table, cameras and robot placement are unchanged.

The RAX dexmate_step tool accepts 1..50 rows, each exactly 16 numbers:
right [world x,y,z, qw,qx,qy,qz, opening], then left with the same eight fields.
Positions are metres in the MuJoCo world, z up. Unit quaternions are active
local-to-world, scalar first wxyz. Optional repeat=1..50 repeats one row;
at most 50 total rows per tool call. Both arms are staged before physics.
Opening is 0 closed, 1 open. Positive commands target 0.96*opening radians;
zero uses the existing bounded closing-torque controller, not a grasp attachment.
Current loaded settings: 0.4 N m closing torque, 0.6 N m maximum gripper torque,
0.25 ms physics timestep, 80 substeps per 20 ms control row (50 Hz). The live
dexmate_status and observation action_layout are authoritative.

TCP sites are 0.16 m along each gripper_base local +z, with the same axes.
These are provisional virtual TCPs, not calibrated grasp centres. Deliberate
orientation changes must use wxyz quaternions. Preserve each arm's own pose
when holding it; all-zero seven-value pose holds its previous reference.
One repeated target may need several chunks to reach it because references
have velocity limits and motion is motor/IK/PD driven. Check actual TCP and
IK residual feedback. Do not mistake a distant unreachable reference for motion.

Tools: dexmate_status (no stepping), dexmate_observe (camera subset allowed,
no stepping), dexmate_step (Cartesian actions), dexmate_hold (hold references),
dexmate_gripper (change openings, hold arms). start_episode starts one reset;
evaluate checks unchanged criteria; finish closes the attempt.

Images: back, ego/head, wrist_left and wrist_right. Proprioception is measured
TCP poses, arm joint positions/velocities, jaw positions, and opening commands.
Hidden object states are operator records, not model observations. There is
no automatically executable fold(panel) skill or planning tool in this adapter.

system.text: You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.
Use only the authorized RAX robot MCP tools for one live box-folding attempt. No files, shell, workers, training, exploration campaign, or benchmark submissions.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__dexmate_gripper
tools.description: Set either or both synchronized jaw openings, holding both current TCP references. 0 closed, 1 open; runs steps * 20 ms.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__dexmate_hold
tools.description: Maintain current TCP and gripper references for steps * 20 ms. Physics continues; returns updated observation.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__dexmate_observe
tools.description: Current camera RGB images and measured robot proprioception. Does not advance physics. Camera subset optional.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__dexmate_status
tools.description: Robot embodiment, exact action layout, cameras, and episode limits. No physics.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__dexmate_step
tools.description: Execute synchronized bimanual absolute TCP actions. Each 16-D row is right [xyz metres, quaternion wxyz, opening 0..1], then left same. One row = 20 ms, both arms at once. Optional repeat repeats a single row, avoiding duplicate JSON; at most 50 executed rows. Returns updated RGB observation.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__evaluate
tools.description: Check the current exploration episode against the task; a success confirms manual success.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__finish
tools.description: Close the current exploration episode. Does not submit. Returns text/image content blocks; images appear directly in the tool result. Never print or stringify image data.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__register
tools.description: Freeze a controller.py bundle without running it; main(ctx) must use only the ctx it is given.

source.description: Project under code/ in your workspace, e.g. code/reach. Rehearsals and the formal batch keep this path.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__rehearse
tools.description: Run the whole registered controller in a fresh exploration episode under the same limits as each formal episode: its step limit and any wall limit (status.episode_timeout_seconds, startup included; null when there is none). Consumes one exploration episode. Returns wall-time breakdown in timing; timeouts identify timeout_stage. Returns text/image content blocks; images appear directly in the tool result. Never print or stringify image data.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__start_episode
tools.description: Start the next exploration episode on the next layout; closes the previous one. Takes no layout or seed arguments. Returns text/image content blocks; images appear directly in the tool result. Never print or stringify image data.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__status
tools.description: Task, manual success evidence, episode state, episode timeout, remaining exploration episodes, registered bundles (rehearsal_qualified: whether each bundle has had a clean rehearsal), workspace storage, and Gemini budgets: total and formal usage.

tools.name: mcp__auto_research__submit
tools.description: One final submission, which closes exploration: freeze the exact cleanly rehearsed bundle for the formal batch (status.formal_episode_count held-out formal episodes); a clean rehearsal ran to its end without errors, whether or not the task succeeded. The formal batch runs it alone after you end your turn, each episode in a fresh sandbox and environment with no agent intervention, code changes or retries; you do not see its result. Each formal episode succeeds or fails by the task condition; the result is the share of successes, and errors and missing evidence count as failures. The formal batch shares the Gemini budget.
